title: Private VPC offline connectivity contract and upgrade acceptance
creator: Ethan Cole
description:
Overview: This ticket defines the connectivity contract, validation tests, and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC customer deployments that operate with zero or highly restricted egress (offline/air-gapped or 'mirror-only' modes). Goal is to produce a deterministic checklist and automated validation suite that Platform and Solutions Engineering can run during onboarding and before upgrades.

Goals:
- Define minimal networking surface and outbound exceptions required for supported Private deployments (full-airgap, mirror-only, limited-egress).
- Specify upgrade choreography that works without outbound access (image mirroring, signature verification, staged rollouts).
- Produce explicit acceptance criteria and test matrix for networking, upgrade dry-runs, and rollback triggers.
- Provide an ops playbook for diagnosing and resolving common connectivity/upgrade failures.

Non-goals:
- Replacing customer's internal network architecture or providing proxy appliances.
- Building an alternative runtime that bypasses customer KMS requirements.

Networking requirements (contract):
- Required inbound control-plane endpoints for private deployments: list of DNS names and ports must be documented in the onboarding artifact. For fully air-gapped mode, control-plane can be disabled; we must support an on-prem control-plane shim.
- Outbound egress: support three operational modes (0) zero-egress: no outbound allowed; (1) mirror-repository-only: outbound allowed to specified mirror IPs/hostnames for artifact pulls; (2) approved-proxy: outbound allowed through a customer-managed proxy with whitelisted destinations.
- Mirror integrity: image and artifact mirrors must serve signed manifests; runtime verifies signature against customer-trusted root CA or preconfigured image signing key.
- Time sync: nodes must allow NTP (or equivalent) to internal NTP server; if external NTP is disallowed, provide instructions for hardware clock drift mitigation.
- DNS: customers can use split-horizon DNS; the deployment must support explicit host overrides for artifact and registry endpoints.

Upgrade choreography and constraints:
- Offline upgrade path: images and packages are mirrored to customer registry. The platform provides a signed release bundle that can be imported. Upgrade verification must succeed without outbound calls.
- Image provenance: every upgrade bundle must include checksum, signature, and release notes. Verification is required locally before applying.
- Staged rollout: support for node-level canary by applying upgrade to a single GPU pool or single node with health checks. Canary must include KV-cache migration checks and warm-start validation.
- Rollback: automatic rollback triggers on a configurable set of SLO breaches (CPU/GPU OOMs, increased token latency by >25% for 5m, sustained error rate >2%). Rollback must be possible without contacting external registries (using cached previous bundle).

Acceptance criteria (must be met before marking Done):
1) Networking validation: automated validator (runbook tool) can correctly classify customer's network mode (zero-egress | mirror-only | proxy) and report missing firewall rules or DNS entries in under 20 minutes.
2) Offline upgrade dry-run: given a mirrored bundle in a customer registry, an upgrade dry-run completes successfully in a test cluster with no outbound access and exits with 0 plus structured report listing: images verified, signatures validated, preflight checks passed.
3) Rollback verification: simulated canary failure triggers rollback flow within configured time window and recovers to previous bundle; validation logs captured and stored locally.
4) Security: image signature verification uses customer-provided trust anchor; cryptographic verification must be demonstrable in logs and artifacts (signed-manifest chain).
5) Observability: Console shows per-node upgrade status and exposes offline deployment health metrics (local logs ingestion, artifact verification status). For private deployments with disabled control plane, a downloadable JSON status snapshot must be available.
6) Playbook & runbook: Completed ops playbook for common failure modes (mirror sync failure, signature mismatch, node clock drift, proxy misconfiguration), reviewed and approved by Security and SRE.

Test matrix (examples):
- Mode A (zero-egress): preflight must fail fast on missing mirrored bundle; dry-run simulates import of bundle via local registry; all checks run locally.
- Mode B (mirror-only with stale mirror): validator detects checksum mismatch and flags remediation steps.
- Mode C (proxy with TLS interception): validate behavioral equivalence and ensure signing chain unaffected.

Telemetry & Traceability:
- Each upgrade attempt must produce a machine-readable deployment-artifact (artifact-id, bundle-sha256, signer-id, timestamp, node-list, result).
- Retain local upgrade logs for 90 days by default (configurable).

Operational playbook highlights:
- Steps to validate mirror sync: compare upstream bundle manifest checksum to mirror manifest; retry strategy with exponential backoff and operator alert thresholds.
- Signature mismatch remediation: instruct to import correct signing key or re-mirror signed bundle; include offline verification commands.
- Nightly sync verification job (optional) that runs locally to assert mirror freshness.

Artifacts & references:
- Onboarding checklist (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PD/pages/Private+Deploy+Onboard+Checklist (draft)
- Draft runbook and validator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-validator (PR#412 pending)
- Example mirrored bundle format & spec: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/private-bundle-specs

Open questions / trade-offs recorded:
- Q1: Do we require signed manifests for every customer mirror? Trade-off: strict security vs operational friction for customers with legacy registries. Current leaning: require signing for GA; provide a transition mode for early customers.
- Q2: Should we provide an optional lightweight proxy appliance? Trade-off: faster onboarding vs increased maintenance surface. Decision deferred to Q2 roadmap discussion.

Decision log (summary):
- 2025-02-14: Chose three-mode networking model (zero-egress, mirror-only, approved-proxy). Owner: Maya.
- 2025-02-20: Image signing required for GA upgrades; transition mode allowed for pilot customers. Owner: Security (Lina Chen).

Next steps / action items:
- Implement validator enhancements: add mirror checksum comparison, signature verification. Assignee: ENG-Infra team (ticket ENG-19822). Target: 2025-02-28.
- Finalize runbook and have Security review sign-off. Assignee: Maya. Target: 2025-03-05.
- Build demo checklist and onboarding artifact for Solutions Eng. Assignee: Ethan. Target: 2025-03-10.
